title: quantization-nan-scratchpad-maya-2026-03-05
summary: Working notes for NaN/quality regressions when running INT8/FP8 quantized variants on 13B transformer. Logs, commands tried, hypotheses and next steps.
content:
Context:
- Model: rlnet-13b (transformer; fused flash attention kernel available)
- Problem: Intermittent NaNs in logits / token probs and occasional `loss=nan` during short inference/eval runs when using INT8 and FP8 quantization profiles. BF16 mode rarely shows NaNs but quality varies.
- Repro window: started seeing consistent NaNs after model conversion changes on 2026-03-02 (quantization pipeline updates: per-channel scaling + new symmetric int8 codepath).
- Ticket: JIRA-QUANT-1245 (tracking).

What I've observed (high-level):
- NaNs appear only when using the fast fused attention + int8 matmul kernels (both per-channel and per-tensor).
- Using slower fallback kernels (float32 or bf16 matmul) removes NaNs.
- NaNs often appear after the first few tokens (starts clean then NaN at decode step 8-25).
- Traceback pinpoints softmax/attention scores or eventual gelu outputs being NaN; sometimes LayerNorm outputs NaN.

Commands / runs tried (notes inline):
1) Baseline FP32 (control):
   CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python run_eval.py --model rlnet-13b --dtype fp32 --batch 1 --seq 256
   -> clean; no NaNs; perf baseline 120 tokens/s

2) INT8 quantize (new pipeline):
   CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python quantize.py --model rlnet-13b --qtype int8 --per_channel true --calib_data ./calib/1000.jsonl --out model-int8.pt
   python run_eval.py --model model-int8.pt --dtype int8 --batch 1 --seq 256
   -> NaN occurs ~step 12. Log snippet:
      [2026-03-04 14:03:22] INFO step 11: token_loss 0.0042
      [2026-03-04 14:03:22] INFO step 12: token_loss NaN
      stack: attention_softmax -> matmul -> kernel_fused_int8 -> dispatch

3) INT8 + fallback for attention kernel (force fp32 / bf16 for attn):
   CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python run_eval.py --model model-int8.pt --force-attn-fallback bf16
   -> No NaNs. Performance down ~30%. Implication: fused int8 attention kernel likely culprit.

4) FP8 experimental profile:
   python quantize.py --model rlnet-13b --qtype fp8 --format e4m3 --calib_data ./calib/500.jsonl
   run_eval with FP8 kernels -> Intermittent NaNs, less frequent than INT8 but still present.

5) BF16 mixed-mode (matmul bf16, LayerNorm/softmax fp32):
   -> stable; suggests precision of softmax/layernorm / scale factors matter.

6) Per-tensor vs per-channel experiments:
   - per_channel true -> more NaNs (surprising), per_channel false -> fewer NaNs but quality worse in some prompts.

Debug / logs (excerpts):
- attention scores before softmax: [12.3, 11.9, NaN, 14.1] -> indicates intermediate overflow/inf or invalid compute in matmul output
- layernorm input: [0.12, -0.02, NaN] -> sometimes LN introduces NaN when denom ~0 and eps small
- kernel error: device-side assert in fused_kernel_int8.cu (line approx 342) observed occasionally

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Scaling/clipping mismatch during calibration -> quant scale too small or too large causing overflow to inf/NaN in int8 matmul (most likely).
   - Evidence: fallback to fp32/bf16 fixes it, per-channel scaling changes incidence rate.
2) Fused attention/int8 kernel has a bug (edge cases) where accumulation uses insufficient accumulator precision (int32 overflow) or incorrect sign handling for asym vs sym quantization.
   - Evidence: device-side assert in kernel, starts after non-trivial sequence length when accumulation grows.
3) LayerNorm/softmax numerical instability after quantized matmul -> small variance and eps handling could produce division by ~0.
   - Evidence: NaN sometimes shows in LN inputs; increasing LN eps reduced frequency in one experiment.
4) Calibration dataset mismatch -> calibration not covering rare activation ranges (causes underflow/overflow on long sequences).

Commands/probes to test hypotheses (what I ran and next to run):
A) Print per-tensor/per-channel scales during quantize step and add asserts for zeros/NaNs:
   python - <<EOF
import torch, json
sc = torch.load('model-int8.pt', map_location='cpu')['scales']
# print shapes and min/max
print('scales_min', min([s.min().item() for s in sc]))
print('scales_max', max([s.max().item() for s in sc]))
EOF
   -> scales min>0 but some extremely small: 1.2e-06 -> may cause very large inverse/saturation in dequant multiplies.

B) Add clamp after dequant before matmul to bound values (quick hack):
   - insert torch.clamp(x, -1e4, 1e4) before softmax; reduces NaN frequency but not eliminated.

C) Switch quantizer to asymmetric per-tensor and re-run calibration with 2k examples:
   python quantize.py --qtype int8 --per_channel false --asymmetric true --calib_data ./calib/2000.jsonl
   -> fewer NaNs but still present on long sequences >512 tokens.

D) Increase LayerNorm eps from 1e-5 to 1e-3 in the runtime wrapper for quantized models:
   -> dramatically reduced occurrences in a quick pass (promising).

E) Run correctness tests with random seeds and compare FP32 vs INT8 intermediate tensors (capture QKV pre-softmax):
   - script: capture_intermediates.py -> dump qkv_fp32.npy and qkv_int8_dequant.npy and diff
   -> diffs very large for some channels; pattern: a few channels show huge gain -> those correspond to tiny scales.

F) Kernel debug: build with assertions and run under cuda-memcheck to get exact failing index for device assert.

Quick notes about calibration & scales: 
- The calibrator uses max-abs per-channel with outlier clipping 99.999 percentile. That clipping might remove rare but valid high activations and produce tiny scales for other channels. Consider using KL-divergence or MSE-based scaling or increase percentile to 99.9999 or apply stability floor on scale.
- Also need to ensure embedding/positional biases are included in calibration data; earlier calibrations used only 1k random prompts mostly short (<=32 tokens).

Temporary mitigations we can deploy to customers: 
- Force attention kernel to fallback to bf16 on Dedicated until fixed (config flag in serving runtime per-model).
- Increase LN eps to 1e-3 for quantized models by default.
- Add guard clamping around softmax logits to clip extreme values before softmax (e.g., torch.clamp(logits, -1e3, 1e3)).

Next steps (action list):
- [ ] Reproduce deterministically with a small synthetic prompt that triggers NaN reliably and attach to ticket (target: deterministic repro by 2026-03-07)
- [ ] Add additional logging in quantize.py to emit per-layer scale histograms during calibration
- [ ] Run cuda-memcheck + kernel assertions to find exact failure indices in fused int8 attention kernel (assign to Ethan)
- [ ] Try alternative calibrator (KL/MSE) and floor scales at 1e-4 to avoid tiny scales
- [ ] Add unit test that compares FP32 intermediate QKV -> dequantized outputs within eps for most channels and flags channels with >1e3 difference
- [ ] Draft short mitigation note for Ops/Customer Success to rollout fallback config and LN eps bump (Lina to own)

Breadcrumbs / chat links: 
- Slack: #quantization "maya: observed NaNs with new int8 fused kernel" (2026-03-04)
- PR with quantizer change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/987
- JIRA: JIRA-QUANT-1245

Notes to self (observational):
- When in doubt, fallback to higher-precision for normalization/softmax and keep matmul quantized. Most numerics break downstream of normalization/softmax.
- Per-channel theoretically better, but calibration and scale stability matter more in practice.

Short-term experiments to schedule (priority):
1) Bruteforce increase scale floor (1e-4) + per-tensor asymmetric quant + 5k calibration -> measure NaN frequency.
2) Kernel assert run + exact failing index -> will show if accumulation overflow or indexing bug.
3) Softmax/clamp + LN eps bump as stopgap.

Raw console snippets (for reference):
- NaN log example:
  [2026-03-04 14:03:22] ERROR eval_step 12: output probs NaN
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "kernel_launcher.cu", line 342, in fused_int8_attention
    -> device side assert: index out of range (maybe in shared memory tile index?)

- Debug compare dump (partial):
  qkv_fp32[0,3,:8] = [0.12, -1.1, 2.3, 0.0, 0.003, 1.2, -0.2, 0.04]
  qkv_int8_dequant[0,3,:8] = [1.2e4, -1.1, inf, 0.0, 0.003, -inf, -0.2, 0.04]

If I don't have time tomorrow: leave kernel assert + cuda-memcheck to Ethan, Lina to prepare customer-facing mitigation note. I'll keep iterating on calibrator parms and LN eps.

End of scratchpad.
